1
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/ in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 02.09.2021 at about 11.30 a.m he was pushing his cart loaded with vegetables on the extreme left side of the road near Sambhrama College, M.Palya,
Vidyaranyapura Post, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Car bearing Regn.No.KA01MA1172 came from Sambhrama College, Ambabavani Temple came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed petitioner and caused accident.
Due to the impact, he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Nagappa Hadi hospital, M.S.Palya Circle, Vidyaranyapura Post, Bangalore, by the public at the spot, wherein after first aid treatment he was shifted to K.C.General hospital, and the xray reveals that petitioner has sustained multiple left rib fracture, with multiple abrasion over face, right hand, left shoulder and left thigh and (SCCH12) 3 MVC No.4310/2021 he underwent surgery.
He has spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance, food and nourishment charges and other expenses.
He is suffering from permanent disability as he is not able to do any work.
Prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was selling vegetables by pushing the cart and earning Rs.1,000/ per day.
After the accident, he is not able to do any work and lost his entire earnings.
The injuries sustained have caused permanent disability.
The accident is solely due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing Regn.No.KA01 MA1172.
The Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered case in Crime No.147/2021 for the offence p/u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the R.C owner and respondent no.2 is the insurer of opponent vehicle are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/ with interest and costs in the above case.
3. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 remained absent to the court, hence he was placed exparte.
Respondent no.2 appeared before this court through his counsel and has filed written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
He further submitted that there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint.
That the 1st respondent being the owner of the car having sold the said car to accused driver have colluded with petitioner to claim unlawful gain.
Further it has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Car bearing Regn.No.KA01MA1172 in favour of 1 st respondent.
That the liability of this respondent if any, is (SCCH12) 4 MVC No.4310/2021 subject to terms and conditions of policy.
That the said accident has occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner who had ventured into selling vegetables on the push cart without observing the coming vehicles.
There is 75% of contribution in negligence by the petitioner in causing the accident.

Further the driver of the insured Car bearing Regn.No.KA01MA1172 i.e.,
the owner had entrusted the said car to an unlicensed driver.
The driver of the vehicle at the time of accident was under the influence of alcohol, and also has violated the terms and conditions of policy and M.V.Act.
That, the amount claimed as compensation is baseless, speculative, imaginary and exorbitant and this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
The age, occupation, income and permanent disability of the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors inoffice has framed following:

1. Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 02.09.2021due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Regn.No.KA01MA 1172 which dashed to the petitioner while he was pushing the cart loaded with vegetable near Sambhrama College, M.S.Palya, Bangalore.?
Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that the driver of car Car bearing Regn.No.KA01MA 1172 did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
5. To prove his case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.22 documents are marked.
On the the hand, the authorized representative of respondent no.2 is examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 to R.3 are marked and respondent evidence is closed.

sentences.text: To prove his case petitioner entered himself into witness box and got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has reiterated petition averments.

He produced FIR, first information, charge sheet, sketch,spot mahazar, wound certificate and IMV report, IMV report, wound certificate, final report and discharge summary at Ex.P.1 to 6 and 8.
9.
As per the first information petitioner himself is first informant.
He gave the information to police after 2 days of the accident.
He stated that, he was pushing the cart to sell the vegetables and the driver of Car bearing no.KA01MA1172 drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and caused accident.
He also stated that he was taking treatment and therefore delay in filing the complaint.
As per the final report (SCCH12) 7 MVC No.4310/2021 driver of the said car is found to be negligent.
Charge sheet is filed against him for the offence under Section 279, 337 of Ipc by Yelahanka Traffic Police.
As per rough sketch it can be seen that car came from opposite direction and petitioner was on the side of the road with his cart.
As per the wound certificate the injuries found on the body of petitioner is simple in nature.
The driver of the vehicle has not appeared to say anything about the contributory negligence on part of the petitioner.
He is not summoned from the side of respondent no.2 insurance company to prove its defence.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 suggestion that petitioner was pushing the cart in the middle of the road is denied.
The final report is not questioned by the accused driver.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court there is negligence on part of car driver in driving the car.
Accordingly, I hold this issue in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.2 : Respondent no.2 has disputed the age, occupation, income and permanent disability of the petitioner.
To prove his age petitioner has not produced any documents.
In police records, in the first information petitioner mentioned his age as 47 years.
In final report his age is mentioned as 47 years.
In medical bills it is mentioned as 43 years.
In OPD record it is mentioned as 49 years.
Therefore there is difference in the age mentioned in the records produced before this court.
In the cross examination of P.W.1, there is no suggestion in respect of age of the petitioner.

Since petitioner himself has given his age as 47 years at the time of accident in the first (SCCH12) 8 MVC No.4310/2021 information, the same is considered as his appropriate age at the time of accident, in the absence of any contrary evidence by the respondents.
11. Respondent no.2 has disputed the occupation of the petitioner.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner is vegetable vendor and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
But, no documents are produced to show his occupation or income.
Therefore, notional income has to be inferred.

Having regard to the age of the petitioner, year of the accident being 2021, the place of residence of petitioner being Bengaluru Urban, the notional income of petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/ per month.
Hence, the income of the petitioner per month is considered as Rs.14,000/.
To prove permanent disability, petitioner has not got examined any doctor.

Hence,
this court is of the opinion that, petitioner has no permanent disability.

Accordingly I answer this S. Rajesh vs Khaja.D on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34380119/
4 issue Partly in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.3 :

sentences.text: 2nd respondent contended that the driver of car was not having effective D.L at the time of accident.
But, there is no such charge in the final report against the accused.

Further,
2nd respondent got examined his authorized representative as R.W.1.
She has produced notice issued to 1 st respondent owner to produce driving licence of the driver at the time of accident.
She contended that owner has not produced the same and therefore according to 2nd respondent driver had no driving licence.
To prove that Ex.R.3 notice is sent to owner, (SCCH12) 9 MVC No.4310/2021 no document is produced.
Therefore, it cannot be assumed that such notice is sent to owner respondent no.1.
Hence, 2 nd respondent has not proved this issue in his favour.

Accordingly,
I hold this Issue in the Negative.
13. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the car bearing reg.no.KA01MA1172.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained only simple injuries as per the wound certificate.
He has contended that, he suffered rib fracture by the accident.
But, the same is not mentioned in the wound certificate produced by him.
Further he has not produced any discharge summary for taking treatment in respect of the rib fracture.
There is no inpatient record of the petitioner.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded for pain and sufferings, interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, Rs.10,000/ is awarded under this head.
(ii) For Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.9 and 20.
They are disputed by the respondents.
Petitioner has not calculated the bills produced by him.

In the cross examination of P.W.1 those medical bills are disputed, but no satisfactory material is forthcoming to disbelieve the bills.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.68,136/ towards medical expenses.
(SCCH12) 11 MVC No.4310/2021 (iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner has not produced inpatient records.
Hence, food and nourishment charges cannot be awarded.
(iv) For Attendant charges: The petitioner has not produced inpatient records.
Hence, attendant charges cannot be awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.14,000/.
To recover from simple injury one month is required in the opinion of this court.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total one month.
He is entitled to Rs.14,000/ as loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to hospital from the spot of accident.
He took treatment at Victoria hospital.
Considering the conveyance, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.3,000/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.3,000/ is awarded.
(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2 there is no permanent or functional disability of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation can be awarded under this head.
Further, there is no evidence to show that future medical treatment is necessary.

Hence,
compensation under future medical expenses is not awarded.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.95,136/ in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
14. Liability: Since respondent no.2 has admitted the insurance policy of car bearing No.KA01 MA1172 which is valid on the date of accident, respondent no.2 is liable to indemnify the insured.

In view of settled law on the point of interest, though petitioner claimed interest at the rate of 12%
pa he is only entitled to 6% interest on the award amount except on future medical expenses.

Hence,
I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
15. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER (SCCH12) 13 MVC No.4310/2021 The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.95,136/ with interest @ 6% pa on the said from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The 2nd respondent is liable to indemnify the insured and 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
After such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation in his favour.

The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Award be drawn accordingly.
